input.prompt: Simulate uniaxial tensile loading of a Copper single crystal using LAMMPS. The crystal should be oriented such that the simulation box axes x, y, and z align with the crystallographic <100> directions of the face-centered cubic (FCC) lattice. Use metal units and define an FCC lattice with a lattice constant of 3.61 Å. Construct a 10×10×10 unit cell simulation box with periodic boundary conditions in all directions. Employ the Embedded Atom Method (EAM) potential for Copper. Equilibrate the system at 300 K and zero pressure isotropically using the NPT ensemble with a Nose-Hoover thermostat and barostat. Use a timestep of 0.001 picoseconds and run equilibration for at least 20 picoseconds. Following equilibration, apply uniaxial tensile deformation along the x-axis at a strain rate of 0.01 ps⁻¹ by deforming the simulation box in the x-direction, while maintaining zero pressure in the transverse y and z directions via NPT dynamics. Continue deformation for 20 picoseconds to capture the material’s mechanical response. Record the strain and corresponding stress components in the format `strain, stress_xx, stress_yy, stress_zz` every 100 timesteps, with stresses saved in GPa. As the final result, report the maximum tensile stress (in GPa) along the x-direction achieved prior to the onset of plastic deformation or structural instability, identified as the first significant drop in the stress-strain response. This is a large simulation, hence it is advisable to use multiple CPUs.

Initialize a 3D Aluminum single crystal in LAMMPS. Use metal units and define a 10×10×10 simulation box in three dimensions. Create a face-centered cubic (FCC) lattice with a lattice constant of 4.05 Å, oriented in the <100> directions along x, y, and z. Set periodic boundary conditions in all directions. Define the atomic type for Aluminum and assign the atomic structure inside the simulation box. Save this structure using the write_data command in LAMMPS in initial_structure.xyz. As the final output, return the absolute path of the structure file. The input script used for this simulation should be named subtask_1.in

You are given the absolute path of the initialized structure of the 3D Aluminum single crystal. Read that structure file and equilibrate the system using an NPT ensemble at a temperature of 300 K and a pressure of 0 bar in all directions using the Nose-Hoover temperature thermostat and Nose-Hoover pressure barostat. Run the equilibration for 20 picoseconds with a timestep of 0.001 picoseconds. Save the equilibrated structure using the write_data command in LAMMPS in equlibrated_structure.xyz, and as the final output, return its absolute path. The input script used for this simulation should be named subtask_2.in

You are given the absolute path of the equilibrated structure of the 3D Aluminum single crystal. Read that structure file and apply uniaxial tensile deformation along the x-direction at a strain rate of 0.01 picosecond⁻¹. Maintain zero pressure in the y and z directions using the NPT ensemble using the Nose-Hoover temperature thermostat and Nose-Hoover pressure barostat. Run the simulation for 20 picoseconds with a timestep of 0.001 picoseconds. Save stress and strain values to a text file every 100 timesteps in a file called stress_strain.txt. The file should include strain, defined as (Lx - L0)/L0, and stress values in the x, y, and z directions, converted from bars to GPa in the format strain,stress_xx,stress_yy,stress_zz without any column names or metadata. As the final output, return the absolute path of this text file. The input script used for this simulation should be named subtask_3.in

You are given the path of the text file which contains the stress-strain values for a material under uniaxial tension. Plot the stress-strain curve and save it as an image file with appropriate x- and y-axis labels. As the final output, give the absolute path for this plot. The input script used for this simulation should be named subtask_4.in
